decisions.executionNote: Basket is on the left; begin a conservative elbow-up left-arm approach and turn the open gripper downward.
Move above the left basket with clearance while finishing the downward approach orientation.
Align the left gripper over the front egg and descend toward a top grasp; keep the right arm parked.
Fine-align and close around the front egg. Retention will be checked visually on lifting.
Lift the first egg clear of the basket with the gripper commanded closed, then start toward the central holder.
The egg remains between the fingers. Carry it over the holder's left-back cup without moving the parked right arm.
The egg has slipped beside the holder. Replan from the interrupted pose, opening and lowering toward that egg with smaller increments.
Move away from the holder rim and align above the slipped egg before further descent; contact caused substantial tracking error.
Use the wrist view to center the open fingers around the table egg; descend gently while staying clear of the holder.
Withdraw from the narrow basket-holder gap and begin turning the gripper so its fingers can approach the loose egg without side collisions.
Reorient above the loose egg, aligning the finger opening with the narrow gap. The holder lid will need reopening before placement.
Approach the table egg from the side of the basket with small translations and a nearly vertical gripper.
Lower slowly toward the loose egg, keeping the open fingers away from the holder edge.
Fine-center the loose egg within the gripper using the wrist view while lowering to its equator.
Basket contact is obstructing the approach. Lift clear and move the actual finger center rightward over the loose egg.
Attempt a slow grasp at the visually aligned loose egg, then make a short lift to check whether it is retained.
The egg is not retained. Open, lift, and make a small wrist-view alignment correction before another approach.
Adjust lateral alignment at clearance height; use the next wrist view to resolve the remaining offset to the egg.
Clear the basket contact and align the fingers with the loose egg using the head view; wrist alignment remains uncertain.
Lower the left gripper carefully over the loose egg. Begin raising and orienting the right arm to reopen the prematurely closed holder.
Move the left fingers slightly clear of the holder and close gently around the loose egg. Continue the right-arm approach above its own workspace.
Release the unsuccessful pinch and withdraw the left fingers from the holder. Bring the right open gripper above the lid's front edge.
Correct the rejected tensor; raise the left arm clear while aligning the right wrist above the holder.
Bring the right open fingers toward the lid's front rim while keeping the left arm clear above the basket.
Lower the right fingers to the lid perimeter and pinch its sides near the front, keeping the basket arm stationary.
Test a controlled upward lift of the lid front, keeping the right gripper closed and monitoring whether the base stays on the table.
The lid was not retained. Turn the right gripper to pinch across its front lip, while aligning the left gripper with a basket egg.
Make a controlled left pinch near the basket egg; finish turning the right fingers across the lid's front rim.
Advance the right fingers across the front lid edge and pinch; move the left open gripper further over the basket rather than its rim.
Test the right front-rim pinch by lifting along the lid-opening direction; lower the left open fingers further into the basket.
Close the left fingers around the centered basket egg after a small descent. Reapproach the lid lip lower with the right gripper open.
Make short retention-check lifts: keep the left egg pinch closed, and close the right gripper on the lid edge before lifting.
The left egg was not retained; approach farther into the basket before closing again. Continue a small right lid-edge lift to check engagement.
The lid is now opening. Continue its controlled arc with the right hand; make a small left alignment correction and close around the basket egg.
Withdraw the right hand from the opened lid and test whether the left egg is retained on a vertical lift.
The prior action was rejected without motion. Use smaller right-arm withdrawal increments and lift the left pinch for a visual retention check.
Reposition the left grasp toward the near side of the basket egg and straighten the approach. Park the right hand clear of the reopened holder.
Fine-center the basket egg between the left fingers and close at a fixed height before testing retention.
Lift straight up with the left gripper closed and verify the egg stays between the fingers before transporting.
The egg stayed in the basket. Descend with open fingers to a deeper equatorial grasp rather than closing above it.
The egg is centered between the open pads. Lower slightly to surround its body, then close without lateral motion.
Correct toward the near side of the egg, which shifted forward during closure; reopen, recenter, and test a short closed-gripper lift.
Lift the centered egg vertically, maintaining the closed command and checking its position relative to the fingers.
The egg is visibly retained during the lift. Carry it toward the near-left cup while withdrawing the right arm for clearance.
The transported egg is no longer visible in the fingers. Withdraw and inspect the area before another slower, deeper grasp.
Approach the loose egg using the head-view position and link-to-finger offset, stopping above the table for alignment.
Lower around the table egg and narrow the opening enough to clear the adjacent holder rim.
Use the wrist view to move the loose egg toward the center of the open pads without descending further.
The adjacent holder obstructs lateral alignment. Lift clear and turn the left opening along the gap before returning to the loose egg.
Finish aligning the fingers along the narrow gap at increased clearance before a new vertical approach.
Approach the loose egg with fingers oriented along the gap, accounting for the link-to-finger offset and keeping the holder clear.
Descend vertically around the loose egg while preserving the narrow-gap orientation; stop short of the table for a grasp check.
Close the left fingers at the head-view-aligned loose egg and make a short vertical lift; the wrist camera is occluded by the basket.
Lift vertically to clear the basket occlusion and check whether the loose egg was actually captured before any transport.
The egg remains on the table. Reopen and correct the wrist-view offset while descending cautiously, checking for basket obstruction.
The basket blocks this loose-egg approach. Withdraw upward and return to an unobstructed basket egg with the original grasp orientation.
Align a near-vertical open grasp above the basket's front egg, away from the holder obstruction.
Center the front basket egg in the left wrist view and descend to a deeper grasp height with the fingers open.
Adjust the pads slightly toward the near side and lower to surround the front egg's body, then close without moving.
Test retention with a slow vertical lift and keep the closed command; do not begin transport until the egg visibly follows.
The egg appears to follow the fingers. Continue a slow straight lift to clear the basket, preserving orientation and the closed command.
The egg is retained. Add rim clearance and begin a very slow translation toward the holder, keeping orientation fixed.
Carry the visibly retained egg slowly toward the holder at constant height and orientation, with clearance from the basket rim.
Continue the slow level transfer; the egg remains fixed between the fingers in the wrist view.
Maintain the stable closed grasp and slow lateral motion toward the holder's near-left cup.
Continue the slow, level transfer with the egg visibly retained. Keep both arms separated and the right hand stationary.
Approach the near-left holder cup slowly, adjusting slightly toward its front row while maintaining the stable egg grasp.
Align the retained egg over the near-left cup and lower slowly toward seating height, keeping the grip closed.
The egg is centered above the near-left cup. Seat it gently and open the fingers while holding position.
The wrist view suggests the egg is at the cup's front edge rather than centered. Resecure it before shifting slightly farther into the holder.
The egg now appears inside the near-left cup. Open and withdraw clear of it, returning toward the basket for the remaining eggs.
One egg is visibly seated with the gripper open. Return above the basket's right remaining egg using the stable grasp orientation.
